As there are [more](https://github.com/siacs/Conversations/tree/jingle) and [more](https://siskin.im/) XMPP clients that do have native Jingle audio/video calling I'd like to invite a participant knowing their JID to avoid the need to install separate Jitsi app.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like to have additional option: `Invite by JID` where I'd put the JID in question and have that person invited. (This could also check in contact book for contacts that do have Jabber field filled in).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The only alternative is to ask them to install Jitsi Meet or to use phone calling.

Allowing other XMPP clients to dial-in to Meet would help interoperability between clients!

Thank you for you work and time!

Thank you for your detailed feedback regarding the auto-upload behavior. We understand how important subdirectory support and two-way synchronization are for your workflow. 

Regarding the app crashing when attempting to create folders during auto-upload setup, this was tracked in issue #5454 (https://github.com/nextcloud/android/issues/5454) and has been closed as resolved. We appreciate your patience as we continue to improve the app's synchronization capabilities.

REAL USER REVIEW:
I kinda like that you have to be real particular about selecting folders to upload, but until there's an auto-sync, I'll be using Syncthing. a little more detail: you can select "auto-upload" and specify a local folder, a remote folder, and some other stuff (defaults are probably fine). It will then _upload_ _new_ files in that local directory (but not subdirectories, which is important for music). So all those existing files, never touched. And if you delete a file, that doesn't propagate out to your server, and therefore to your other devices. And if a file is changed/created/etc on the server, you'll never know about it until you manually sync that folder.

- Issue body excerpt: It seems there are two ways how to optimize the Background Blur feature.

improve default HTTPS security

- Tracker: jitsi/jitsi-meet (GitHub)
- Issue #5768: improve default HTTPS security
- Binary state: closed
- URL: https://github.com/jitsi/jitsi-meet/issues/5768
- Issue body excerpt: ## Description
Especially since we move JVB2 to stable and configure NGINX the HTTPS setup is suboptimal.
In fate of Zoom's (fake) encryption disasters we can show our open source community muscles ;)

## Current behavior
Insecure protocols like TLS1.0/TLS1.1 and old ciphers are configured with Debian packages.
With NGINX they also overwrite downstream defaults in http context via server in vhost.

## Expected Behavior
Provide a secure defaults for HTTPS that support newer browser and clients but not legacy.
Most user will blindly install and need shipped defaults for easy but secure adoption .

## Possible Solution
Optimize vhost examples and generate DH parameter in jitsi-meet-web-config.postinst

## Steps to reproduce
Install Jitsi Debian packages on supported Ubuntu LTS or Debian releases and check HTTPS.

# Environment details
Should be relevant for all Debian packages targets but was spotted with Ansible on bionic.
